I don't have NAS-Bench-201 accuracy tables in this environment, so these are priors from general knowledge of the search space, not measured interaction effects. Most interaction claims need a consistent, practically meaningful effect across all three datasets, which is a demanding bar, so I've kept most probabilities low. Claims that replace a `none` edge (5, 12) get somewhat higher numbers, since turning a disconnected edge on usually gives a large, reliable gain.
